findings.problem: PowerShell function name regex does not match hyphenated function names. 'function\s+(\w+(\-\w+)*)' only captures characters before the first hyphen.
findings.root_cause: In .NET regex, \w does not match '-'. The pattern (\w+(\-\w+)*) matches 'Get' from 'Get-MyFunc' because the hyphen terminates the \w+ match and the inner (\-\w+) isn't consumed.
findings.impact: Repo graph indexer misses PowerShell functions with hyphens in names (the naming convention), producing incomplete dependency graphs
findings.evidence: repo-graph.ps1 line 174: regex 'function\s+(\w+(\-\w+)*)'. Tested: 'function Get-MyFunc' would capture 'Get' not 'Get-MyFunc'.
findings.recommended_fix: Change regex to 'function\s+([\w\-]+)' which matches hyphens within the capture group

findings.problem: Index-Symbols line number calculation uses O(n) array allocation (1..N) for what should be O(1) newline counting
findings.root_cause: Expression '(1..($content.Substring(0, $m.Index).Split("`n").Count))[-1]' creates full integer array purely to extract count
findings.impact: For large files, unnecessary memory allocation during symbol indexing
findings.evidence: repo-graph.ps1 line 183: unnecessary 1..N array creation in line number calculation
findings.recommended_fix: Replace with ($content.Substring(0, $m.Index) -split '`n').Count

findings.problem: Example finding schema shows risk_score: 1 as a numeric value. LLM agents may copy this literal value instead of computing actual risk scores.
findings.root_cause: Template uses risk_score: 1 as a placeholder without indicating it must be computed
findings.impact: Findings produced by LLM agents following this template may all have risk_score=1, degrading prioritization accuracy
findings.evidence: independent-auditor.md line 14: 'risk_score: 1' in example JSON output schema
findings.recommended_fix: Replace 'risk_score: 1' with 'risk_score: <compute from Impact x Likelihood x Exposure x Detectability>'
